New York to look up his sister, so I did and they had an extra room in the back, that's where I stayed with the sister. I happened to hang around the Rhythm Club and I made my contacts there and I'd get a gig there once in a while and I ran into a fella now that's doing "One Mo' Time" by the name of Jabbo Smith, one of the trumpet greats.

There used to be a band in Newark Jabbo and I used to go to to play with gigs, you know, play around. One time we were playing at the ballroom in Orange, New Jersey and this fella walked---danced by--- he kept looking at me and he kept looking at Jab and looking at the other guy, and he was getting loaded and I'd see him breaking and I'd see him dance by -- he was a white fella -- he'd dance by and he'd stop and look at me again and then go dance by so the next time he danced by he stopped and looked at me…

says, "See that guy next to me over there, the guitar player?" Willie. Willie was awfully dark, he was very, very dark. So he told this white fella, he says, "See that guitar player over there, he's Indian, too." So this fella moved over to where Willie was playing his guitar and looked him straight in the eye and slowly shook his head, "Oh, no, he's not Indian."
